Package com.codedstream.otterstream.jdbc

Class JdbcFeatureProvider

java.lang.Object
com.codedstream.otterstream.jdbc.JdbcFeatureProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
FeatureProvider
public class JdbcFeatureProvider extends Object implements FeatureProvider
FeatureProvider backed by a JDBC-accessible table: one row per entity, one column per feature. Depends only on java.sql — bring whatever JDBC driver (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, Redshift, ...) you need on the runtime classpath yourself.

Expected data shape:

A table such as: 
 CREATE TABLE user_features (
   user_id      VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,
   age          INT,
   country      VARCHAR,
   ltv_score    DOUBLE PRECISION
 );

Usage:


 // simplest: a raw JDBC URL, a new Connection opened per fetch()
 JdbcFeatureProvider features = new JdbcFeatureProvider(
         "jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/features", "reader", "secret",
         "user_features", "user_id");

 // production: bring your own pooled DataSource (HikariCP, etc.)
 JdbcFeatureProvider features = new JdbcFeatureProvider(myDataSource, "user_features", "user_id");

 Map<String, Object> values = features.fetch("42", List.of("age", "country", "ltv_score"));

SQL injection note: entityId is always sent as a bind parameter (never concatenated). table, entityIdColumn, and the featureNames passed to fetch(java.lang.String, java.util.List<java.lang.String>) are interpolated directly into the generated SQL as identifiers — these must come from trusted, developer-supplied configuration, never from end-user input.

Since:
0.1.0

  • Constructor Details

    • JdbcFeatureProvider

      public JdbcFeatureProvider(String jdbcUrl, String username, String password, String table, String entityIdColumn)
      Opens a new Connection via DriverManager on every fetch(java.lang.String, java.util.List<java.lang.String>) call. Simple and dependency-free, but not pooled — fine for low/moderate QPS or prototyping; for production throughput, prefer the DataSource-based constructor with a pooled implementation such as HikariCP.
      Parameters:
      jdbcUrl - JDBC connection URL (its driver must already be on the classpath)
      username - database username
      password - database password
      table - table (or view) to query — trusted config, not user input
      entityIdColumn - column identifying the entity — trusted config, not user input

    • JdbcFeatureProvider

      public JdbcFeatureProvider(DataSource dataSource, String table, String entityIdColumn)
      Uses a caller-supplied, already-configured DataSource (recommended for production — typically a connection pool). This provider never closes the DataSource; the caller retains ownership of its lifecycle.
      Parameters:
      dataSource - a configured JDBC data source
      table - table (or view) to query — trusted config, not user input
      entityIdColumn - column identifying the entity — trusted config, not user input

      public Map<String,Object> fetch(String entityId, List<String> featureNames) throws Exception
      Fetches one row for entityId and returns the requested columns as a map.
      Specified by:
      fetch in interface FeatureProvider
      Parameters:
      entityId - the entity id to look up (bound as a SQL parameter)
      featureNames - the columns to select; if null or empty, every column is selected
      Returns:
      a map of column name to value, or an empty map if no row matched
      Throws:
